links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM scores across repeated generations
links.effect: Repeat-generation analysis showed high test-retest agreement across generations (ICC=0.90; 95% CI, 0.82-0.94).
links.quote: Repeat-generation analysis showed high test-retest agreement across generations (ICC=0.90; 95% CI, 0.82-0.94).

links.outcome: Overconfident reasoning errors in LLM TDM responses
links.effect: Overconfident reasoning was the most common error category (45.4% of total error appearances); models differed significantly on uncertainty acknowledgment (Holm-adjusted p≤0.02).
links.quote: Overconfident reasoning was the most common error category (45.4% of total error appearances).

links.outcome: LLM performance on pharmacokinetic reasoning and management for phenytoin and digoxin
links.effect: High performance on level interpretation and toxicity assessment; significant between-model differences on pharmacokinetic reasoning and management (Holm-adjusted p≤0.02). Claude 94.9% vs ChatGPT 84.5% and Gemini 83.4%.
links.quote: All models showed high performance on level interpretation and toxicity assessment, but significant between-model differences emerged on pharmacokinetic reasoning, management, monitoring, and uncertainty acknowledgment (all Holm-adjusted p≤0.02).

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance and error modes on structured clinical vignettes of therapeutic drug monitoring without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
